replacements.old: Open Enrollment for the 2026 plan year runs November 1, 2025 through January 15, 2026. The changes this year are smaller than in recent years, but the subsidy math has shifted in ways that catch many families off guard.
replacements.new: Open Enrollment for the 2027 plan year runs November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 on HealthCare.gov. Enroll by December 15 for coverage that starts January 1; if you enroll December 16 through January 15, coverage starts February 1 (HealthCare.gov dates and deadlines, checked November 27, 2026). States that run their own marketplace can set different dates.

replacements.old: The big picture for 2026
replacements.new: The big picture for 2027

replacements.old: Enhanced premium tax credits — the expanded ACA subsidies that came from the American Rescue Plan and were extended through the Inflation Reduction Act — remained in place through the 2025 plan year. That means for 2026 Open Enrollment, most middle-income families still qualify for some subsidy assistance.
replacements.new: The IRS says that in general, the premium tax credit is for households with income of at least 100 percent but no more than 400 percent of the federal poverty line for their family size. For tax years 2021 through 2025, Congress temporarily removed the 400 percent limit (IRS premium tax credit questions and answers, page reviewed September 21, 2026).

replacements.old: Whether enhanced subsidies continue past 2025 is a political question that hasn't been settled. The current law expires at the end of 2025 unless Congress acts. We'll update guidance as the situation clarifies.
replacements.new: Your exact plan prices and savings for 2027 depend on your household and income. HealthCare.gov shows them when you fill out a Marketplace application (HealthCare.gov: lower costs).

replacements.new: Open Enrollment for the 2027 plan year runs November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 on HealthCare.gov. Enroll by December 15 for coverage that starts January 1. States that run their own marketplace can set different dates.

replacements.new: If you don't enroll by January 15 (on HealthCare.gov; state-run marketplaces can set different dates), you're generally locked out

replacements.new: Most states we serve use HealthCare.gov. Six run their own marketplace, so make sure you're shopping on the right platform for your state. This list follows CMS's report for the 2026 plan year (CMS 2026 Open Enrollment report, December 5, 2025):
